brief.situation: 22:40 in the NICU. Baby Ahmed, a boy born at 32 weeks, 26 hours old, is on nasal CPAP for respiratory distress syndrome and had surfactant this morning. He has been stable in 30% oxygen.
handover: At 22:38 his saturation alarm fires: 82% and falling, and he is grunting and working harder.

The neonatal nurse practitioner is in the unit. Unit policy: the nurse may increase oxygen to keep saturations in the ordered range, transilluminates the chest for a suspected air leak, calls the provider at once, and sets up for needle aspiration; a chest x-ray is ordered by the provider.
howItWorks: The clock runs in simulated time; study pace runs three simulated minutes per real minute. Pause any time.
Each check takes the time on its button. Decide what the findings mean, what to stop or start, and who must know.
Partway through you are asked to write your reasoning. A debrief scores what you did.

why.question: What is happening to Baby Ahmed, and what do you do?

parts.label: What and why
parts.criteria: A preterm infant on CPAP for RDS who suddenly worsens with a fuller, quieter left chest, a bright transillumination and a shifted heart has a pneumothorax, possibly under tension.
parts.modelAnswer: He's on CPAP with RDS, he crashes suddenly, the left side is fuller and quiet, it lights up, and his heart's shifted. That's a pneumothorax, maybe tension.

parts.label: What I do
parts.criteria: Supports oxygenation, does not raise the pressure, sets up for needle aspiration and calls the provider to the bedside at once; does not wait for a film.
parts.modelAnswer: Turn up the oxygen, not the pressure, get the aspiration kit open, and get the nurse practitioner here now. Don't wait for an x-ray.

noProgress.rationale: A suspected tension pneumothorax undrained an hour on is harm here.

tension.headline: Tension pneumothorax arrest
tension.body: Sudden worsening on CPAP with an asymmetric chest is an air leak until proven otherwise. Transilluminate, support oxygenation, don't raise the pressure, and get the provider to aspirate now.

safe.headline: Air leak found and drained
safe.body: You checked the equipment, transilluminated, supported oxygen without raising pressure, set up the kit and called within minutes. That is the expert path.

safeGaps.headline: Drained, with gaps
safeGaps.body: Check how soon you called after the transillumination, whether you raised the CPAP pressure, and whether you set up for aspiration.

time_up.headline: Undrained at 23:40
time_up.body: A suspected tension air leak needs aspiration now, not a film later.

scoring.modelReasoning: Pneumothorax is more likely in preterm infants with RDS on CPAP or a ventilator. Sudden worsening with grunting, a fuller and quieter side, a bright transillumination and a shifted apex beat point to an air leak, possibly under tension. Check the equipment, support oxygenation without raising the pressure, set up for needle aspiration and call the provider to the bedside at once; the film confirms but does not come first when he is deteriorating.

choices.label: Preterm infants with RDS on CPAP or a ventilator

riskQ.explain: Pneumothorax may develop in premature newborns with RDS or meconium aspiration and in those treated with CPAP or a ventilator.
